- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak for next 3–7 days.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (≥0.77) but price drops sharply, model underreacts; add 1–3% upward bias to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates prices when sentiment is mixed (0.27–0.53) and recent price is trending down; adjust forecast upward by 1–4% for next 5–10 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion after 2–3 consecutive high prices; apply downward correction of 2–5% if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.80) and model forecast is low, model underestimates volatility; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–7 days.
- When sentiment is low and price is falling, model often fails to anticipate further decline; add 1–3% downward bias for next 5–10 days.
